name: Machine Chest Fly
summary: A seated isolation exercise using a fly machine to target the pectoral muscles through horizontal adduction.

setup: Adjust the seat height so the handles or arm pads align horizontally with the mid-to-lower chest.
Sit back firmly against the back pad with your feet flat on the floor.
Grasp the handles with a slight bend in your elbows and retract your shoulder blades against the pad.
steps: Contract your chest to bring the handles together in an arc in front of your sternum.
Squeeze your pectorals firmly at peak contraction without letting your shoulders roll forward.
Slowly reverse the motion, maintaining the slight elbow bend, until you feel a comfortable stretch across your chest.
Pause briefly under control before beginning the next repetition.
instructions.breathing: Exhale as you bring your hands together in front of your chest; inhale as you slowly return to the stretched position.

common_faults.fault: Overstretching at the bottom of the repetition.
common_faults.correction: Set the starting arm position so you achieve a chest stretch without forcing the shoulders into extreme horizontal extension.

common_faults.fault: Rounding the shoulders forward to finish the movement.
common_faults.correction: Keep your thoracic spine extended and shoulder blades pinned to the back pad throughout the squeeze.

common_faults.fault: Bending and extending the elbows excessively, turning the fly into a press.
common_faults.correction: Maintain a fixed, soft bend in the elbows from start to finish.

precautions: Do not set the starting levers too far back if you have limited shoulder mobility or an anterior shoulder impingement.
